### Load PDF from Base64 String in React-PDF

Source: https://github.com/wojtekmaj/react-pdf/wiki/Frequently-Asked-Questions

To load a PDF from a Base64 encoded string using React-PDF, transform the Base64 string into a Data URL by prepending `data:application/pdf;base64,`. This Data URL can then be passed directly to the `file` prop of the `<Document>` component. Ensure the Base64 string is valid and correctly formatted.

```typescript
import React from 'react';
import { Document, Page } from 'react-pdf';

const base64String = '';

function MyDocument() {
  return (
    <Document file={`data:application/pdf;base64,${base64String}`}>
      <Page pageNumber={1} />
    </Document>
  );
}
```

### Load PDF from Multiple Sources in React

Source: https://context7.com/wojtekmaj/react-pdf/llms.txt

This component allows users to load PDF documents from various sources including URLs, base64 encoded strings, File objects, and Uint8Array. It uses the react-pdf library and requires the pdfjs-dist worker. The component handles file uploads, URL inputs, and base64 data to dynamically load and display PDF pages.

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Document, Page, pdfjs } from 'react-pdf';

pdfjs.GlobalWorkerOptions.workerSrc = new URL(
  'pdfjs-dist/build/pdf.worker.min.mjs',
  import.meta.url,
).toString();

function MultiSourcePDFLoader() {
  const [file, setFile] = useState<string | File | Uint8Array | { url: string } | null>(null);
  const [sourceType, setSourceType] = useState<string>('url');

  function handleFileUpload(event: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>): void {
    const uploadedFile = event.target.files?.[0];
    if (uploadedFile) {
      setFile(uploadedFile);
      setSourceType('file');
    }
  }

  function loadFromURL(): void {
    setFile('https://example.com/sample.pdf');
    setSourceType('url');
  }

  function loadFromBase64(): void {
    // Example base64 data URI
    const base64Data = 'data:application/pdf;base64,';
    setFile(base64Data);
    setSourceType('base64');
  }

  async function loadFromArrayBuffer(): Promise<void> {
    try {
      const response = await fetch('https://example.com/sample.pdf');
      const arrayBuffer = await response.arrayBuffer();
      const uint8Array = new Uint8Array(arrayBuffer);
      setFile(uint8Array);
      setSourceType('arrayBuffer');
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Error loading ArrayBuffer:', error);
    }
  }

  return (
    <div>
      <div style={{ marginBottom: '20px', padding: '15px', background: '#f9f9f9', borderRadius: '5px' }}>
        <h3>Load PDF from:</h3>
        <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: '10px', marginBottom: '10px' }}>
          <button onClick={loadFromURL}>URL</button>
          <button onClick={loadFromBase64}>Base64</button>
          <button onClick={loadFromArrayBuffer}>ArrayBuffer</button>
        </div>
        <div>
          <label>
            Or upload file:
            <input type="file" accept="application/pdf" onChange={handleFileUpload} />
          </label>
        </div>
        <div style={{ marginTop: '10px', fontSize: '12px' }}>
          Current source: <strong>{sourceType}</strong>
        </div>
      </div>

      {file && (
        <Document
          file={file}
          onLoadSuccess={({ numPages }) => console.log(`Loaded ${numPages} pages`)}
          onLoadError={(error) => console.error('Load error:', error)}
          onSourceSuccess={() => console.log('Source retrieved successfully')}
          onSourceError={(error) => console.error('Source error:', error)}
        >
          <Page pageNumber={1} width={600} />
        </Document>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

export default MultiSourcePDFLoader;

```

### Render PDF Page with React-PDF Document

Source: https://github.com/wojtekmaj/react-pdf/wiki/Frequently-Asked-Questions

To render a PDF page using React-PDF, you must wrap the `<Page>` component within the `<Document>` component. The `<Document>` component provides the necessary context for rendering PDF content, such as a single page or the document outline. Ensure the `file` prop is correctly set with the PDF source.

```typescript
import React from 'react';
import { Document, Page } from 'react-pdf';

function MyDocument() {
  return (
    <Document file="http://example.com/document.pdf">
      <Page pageNumber={1} />
    </Document>
  );
}
```
